_meta.author: Eduventure (original questions)
_meta.note: Final top-up: primary 20 (Maths 10, Science 5, English 5) and secondary 20 (lower-secondary Maths 5 and Science 5, upper-secondary Additional Maths 5 and Biology 5). In review until approved in /admin. Contains answers: never imported by src/.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: What is 9 × 8?
questions.explanation: 9 × 8 = 72. Trick: 10 × 8 = 80, then take away one 8: 80 − 8 = 72.

mistakes.why: 63 is 9 × 7, one group of 9 too few.

questions.alignment: Primary mathematics: multiplication facts (e.g. KSSR Matematik Tahun 3).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: Which fraction is equal to 1/2?
questions.explanation: Multiply the top and bottom of 1/2 by 4: 4/8. Four of eight equal parts is the same as one of two.
questions.alignment: Primary mathematics: fractions (e.g. KSSR Matematik Tahun 3–4).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: How many hundreds are there in 3,000?
questions.explanation: 1,000 is 10 hundreds, so 3,000 is 30 hundreds (30 × 100 = 3,000).

mistakes.why: 3 is the number of thousands; each thousand holds 10 hundreds.

questions.alignment: Primary mathematics: place value (e.g. KSSR Matematik Tahun 3).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: Put these four-digit numbers in order from smallest to largest.
questions.explanation: All have 2 thousands, so compare the hundreds: 0, 0, 1, 9. For the two with 0 hundreds, compare the tens: 2,019 < 2,091.
questions.alignment: Primary mathematics: whole numbers (e.g. KSSR Matematik Tahun 3).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: Select all the even numbers.
questions.explanation: Even numbers end in 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8 and can be split into two equal groups.

wrong.b: 21 ends in 1, so it is odd.
wrong.d: 47 ends in 7, so it is odd.

questions.alignment: Primary mathematics: number (e.g. KSSR Matematik Tahun 1–2).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: A garden bed is a rectangle 7 m long and 3 m wide. What is its area in square metres?
questions.explanation: Area = length × width = 7 × 3 = 21 m².

mistakes.why: 20 m is the perimeter; area multiplies length by width.
Area multiplies the sides; it does not add them.

questions.objective: Calculate the area of a rectangle.
questions.alignment: Primary mathematics: area (e.g. KSSR Matematik Tahun 4).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: True or false: 1 kilogram is the same as 1,000 grams.
questions.explanation: "Kilo" means one thousand, so 1 kilogram = 1,000 grams.

wrong.false: "Kilo" always means 1,000: 1 kilogram = 1,000 grams, 1 kilometre = 1,000 metres.

questions.alignment: Primary mathematics: mass (e.g. KSSR Matematik Tahun 3).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: A box holds 12 eggs. How many eggs are there in 7 boxes?

mistakes.why: 19 adds the numbers; 7 boxes of 12 means multiply.

questions.alignment: Primary mathematics: multiplication (e.g. KSSR Matematik Tahun 3).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: Which number is a multiple of both 3 and 5?
questions.explanation: 15 = 3 × 5, so it is in both the 3 times table and the 5 times table.

wrong.b: 10 is a multiple of 5, but not of 3.
wrong.c: 9 is a multiple of 3, but not of 5.
wrong.d: 8 is a multiple of neither 3 nor 5.

questions.alignment: Primary mathematics: multiples (e.g. KSSR Matematik Tahun 5).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: What is the mathematical word for the answer you get when you multiply two numbers?
questions.explanation: Multiplying gives a product (4 × 5: the product is 20). Adding gives a sum.
questions.alignment: Primary mathematics: multiplication (e.g. KSSR Matematik Tahun 3–4).

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which material is transparent (lets light pass straight through so you can see clearly through it)?
questions.explanation: Clear glass lets almost all light through, which is why windows are made of it.

wrong.b: Wood is opaque: no light passes through.

questions.objective: Classify materials by how they let light through.
questions.alignment: Primary science: light (e.g. KSSR Sains Tahun 3–4).

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: True or false: a shadow forms when an object blocks light.
questions.explanation: Light travels in straight lines. An opaque object stops the light, leaving a dark area behind it: a shadow.

wrong.false: Shadows are made exactly where an object stops light from reaching a surface.

questions.alignment: Primary science: light (e.g. KSSR Sains Tahun 4).

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Select all the mammals.
questions.explanation: Mammals feed their babies milk and breathe air with lungs. Whales, bats and monkeys are all mammals.

wrong.b: Sharks are fish: they breathe through gills.
wrong.d: Penguins are birds: they have feathers and lay eggs.

questions.alignment: Primary science: classification of animals (e.g. KSSR Sains Tahun 3–4).

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: What do we call a young frog that lives in water and has a tail?
questions.explanation: A tadpole hatches from a frog's egg, breathes with gills and swims with its tail before it grows legs.
questions.objective: Name stages of animal life cycles.
questions.alignment: Primary science: life cycles (e.g. KSSR Sains Tahun 2–3).

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Put the stages of a flowering plant's life in order.
questions.explanation: A seed germinates into a seedling, grows into an adult plant that flowers, and the flowers become fruits with new seeds.
questions.objective: Describe the life cycle of a flowering plant.
questions.alignment: Primary science: plants (e.g. KSSR Sains Tahun 2–3).

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Which word is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: "Friend" is spelled f-r-i-e-n-d. A memory trick: a friend is there to the end (frI END).

wrong.b: The i and e are swapped: it is fri-end.
wrong.c: There is an i before the e: fri-end.
wrong.d: It ends in d, not t.

questions.alignment: Primary English: spelling (e.g. KSSR Bahasa Inggeris).

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Select all the verbs (action words).
questions.explanation: Verbs tell us what someone does: run, eat, sleep.

wrong.b: "Happy" is an adjective: it describes a feeling.
wrong.d: "Blue" is an adjective: it describes a colour.

questions.alignment: Primary English: grammar – word classes (e.g. KSSR Bahasa Inggeris).

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: True or false: "quickly" and "slowly" are opposites.
questions.explanation: "Quickly" means at a fast speed and "slowly" means at a low speed, so they are opposites (antonyms).

wrong.false: One means fast and the other means not fast: they are opposites.

questions.alignment: Primary English: vocabulary (e.g. KSSR Bahasa Inggeris).

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Match each animal to the name of its baby.
questions.explanation: A baby cat is a kitten, a baby dog is a puppy and a baby cow is a calf.
questions.alignment: Primary English: vocabulary (e.g. KSSR Bahasa Inggeris).

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Write the plural of "foot": I have two ___.
questions.explanation: "Foot" has an irregular plural: one foot, two feet (like tooth → teeth).
questions.alignment: Primary English: grammar – plurals (e.g. KSSR Bahasa Inggeris).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: What is 3/4 of 120?

mistakes.why: 160 is 120 ÷ 3/4; finding 3/4 of an amount means multiply by 3/4.

questions.objective: Find a fraction of an amount.
questions.alignment: Lower secondary mathematics: rational numbers (e.g. KSSM Matematik Tingkatan 1).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: The point (2, 3) is reflected in the x-axis. Where is its image?
questions.explanation: Reflecting in the x-axis keeps x the same and changes the sign of y.

wrong.b: (−2, 3) is the reflection in the y-axis.
wrong.c: (−2, −3) is a rotation of 180° about the origin.
wrong.d: (3, 2) is the reflection in the line y = x.

questions.objective: Describe reflections on a coordinate plane.
questions.alignment: Lower secondary mathematics: isometric transformations (e.g. KSSM Matematik Tingkatan 2).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: What do the interior angles of any quadrilateral add up to, in degrees?
questions.explanation: A quadrilateral can be split into two triangles: 2 × 180° = 360°.

mistakes.why: 180° is for a triangle; a quadrilateral is two triangles.

questions.objective: Recall the angle sum of a quadrilateral.
questions.alignment: Lower secondary mathematics: polygons (e.g. KSSM Matematik Tingkatan 1).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: Select all the prime numbers.
questions.explanation: A prime number has exactly two factors, 1 and itself: 2, 11 and 17. (2 is the only even prime.)
questions.alignment: Lower secondary mathematics: factors and multiples (e.g. KSSM Matematik Tingkatan 1).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: True or false: −5 is greater than −2.
questions.explanation: On a number line, −5 is further to the left than −2, so −5 is smaller. (A debt of RM5 is worse than a debt of RM2.)

wrong.true: With negatives, the bigger the number after the minus sign, the smaller the value: −5 < −2.

questions.alignment: Lower secondary mathematics: integers (e.g. KSSM Matematik Tingkatan 1).

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which force acts between two surfaces and opposes motion?
questions.explanation: Friction acts where surfaces touch and opposes sliding. It lets us walk without slipping and makes brakes work.

wrong.b: Gravity pulls objects towards each other, such as towards the Earth.
wrong.c: Magnetic force acts between magnets and magnetic materials.
wrong.d: Upthrust is the upward push of a liquid or gas on an object.

questions.alignment: Lower secondary science: forces (e.g. KSSM Sains Tingkatan 2–3).

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: At normal sea-level pressure, at what temperature does pure water boil, in °C?
questions.explanation: Pure water boils at 100 °C at sea level. At high altitude, where pressure is lower, it boils at a lower temperature.

mistakes.why: 0 °C is the freezing (melting) point of water.

questions.alignment: Lower secondary science: matter (e.g. KSSM Sains Tingkatan 1).

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Select all the things produced by aerobic respiration in cells.
questions.explanation: Glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water + energy.

wrong.d: Oxygen is used up by respiration, not produced.
wrong.e: Glucose is broken down by respiration, not produced.

questions.objective: State the word equation for respiration.
questions.alignment: Lower secondary science: respiration (e.g. KSSM Sains Tingkatan 2).

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Put the layers of the Earth in order, from the surface to the centre.
questions.explanation: Crust → mantle → outer core (liquid metal) → inner core (solid metal).
questions.objective: Describe the structure of the Earth.
questions.alignment: Lower secondary science: the Earth (e.g. KSSM Sains Tingkatan 2–3).

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: True or false: acids turn blue litmus paper red.
questions.explanation: Acids turn blue litmus red; alkalis turn red litmus blue.

wrong.false: Blue litmus turning red is the standard test for an acid.

questions.objective: Use indicators to identify acids and alkalis.
questions.alignment: Lower secondary science: acids and alkalis (e.g. KSSM Sains Tingkatan 2).

questions.subject: additional_mathematics
questions.prompt: Given f(x) = 2x + 3, find f⁻¹(7).
questions.explanation: f⁻¹(7) is the x that gives f(x) = 7: 2x + 3 = 7, so x = 2.

mistakes.why: 17 is f(7); the inverse asks which input gives 7.

questions.alignment: Upper secondary additional mathematics: functions (e.g. KSSM Matematik Tambahan Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: additional_mathematics
questions.prompt: What is 180° in radians?
questions.explanation: A full turn is 2π radians = 360°, so a half turn, 180°, is π radians.

wrong.c: π/2 radians is a right angle, 90°.
wrong.d: To convert degrees to radians, multiply by π/180, not by π.

questions.alignment: Upper secondary additional mathematics: circular measure (e.g. KSSM Matematik Tambahan Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: additional_mathematics
questions.prompt: Find the 6th term of the geometric progression 3, 6, 12, …

mistakes.why: 192 is the 7th term; the power is n − 1 = 5, not 6.
That treats it as adding 3 each time; a GP multiplies by r = 2.

questions.objective: Find terms of a geometric progression.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary additional mathematics: progressions (e.g. KSSM Matematik Tambahan Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: additional_mathematics
questions.prompt: True or false: log(a + b) = log a + log b.
questions.explanation: The law is log(ab) = log a + log b: the log of a product, not a sum. For example, log(1 + 1) = log 2, but log 1 + log 1 = 0.

wrong.true: Logs turn multiplication into addition: log(a × b) = log a + log b. There is no simple rule for log(a + b).

questions.objective: Apply the laws of logarithms correctly.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary additional mathematics: indices and logarithms (e.g. KSSM Matematik Tambahan Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: additional_mathematics
questions.prompt: Find the magnitude of the vector 6i + 8j.

mistakes.why: 100 is the magnitude squared; take the square root.

questions.objective: Calculate the magnitude of a vector.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary additional mathematics: vectors (e.g. KSSM Matematik Tambahan Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Through which openings do gases mainly enter and leave a leaf?
questions.explanation: Stomata are tiny pores, mostly on the underside of leaves, opened and closed by guard cells.

wrong.d: The cuticle is a waxy layer that reduces water loss; gases do not pass through it easily.

questions.alignment: Upper secondary biology: plant organs (e.g. KSSM Biologi Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Select all the functions of the liver.
questions.explanation: The liver makes bile, stores glucose as glycogen and detoxifies harmful substances such as alcohol.

wrong.e: Insulin is made by the pancreas.

questions.objective: Describe the functions of the liver.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary biology: homeostasis and organs (e.g. KSSM Biologi / SPM).

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: How many chambers does the human heart have?
questions.explanation: Two atria (upper chambers) and two ventricles (lower chambers).

mistakes.why: There are two sides, each with two chambers: an atrium and a ventricle.

questions.objective: Describe the structure of the heart.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary biology: transport in humans (e.g. KSSM Biologi Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Match each plant structure to its job.

right.text: Carries water and minerals up the plant

questions.explanation: Root hair cells absorb water, xylem carries it upwards, and phloem moves sugars made in the leaves to where they are needed.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary biology: transport in plants (e.g. KSSM Biologi Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: True or false: vaccines contain antigens that stimulate the body to produce antibodies and memory cells.
questions.explanation: A vaccine exposes the immune system to a harmless form of an antigen, so it makes antibodies and memory cells and can respond quickly to the real pathogen later.

wrong.false: That is how vaccines work: they train the immune system using antigens without causing the disease.

questions.alignment: Upper secondary biology: immunity (e.g. KSSM Biologi Tingkatan 4 / SPM).
